chief_complaint: wrist pain and tingling in her fingers
hpi_details: gradual onset of numbness, tingling, and burning pain in her right hand over the past two months. Affects the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Worse at night, often waking her up, and during long typing sessions at work. Eased by shaking her hand ('flick sign'). No pain in the neck, elbow, or shoulder. Normal grip strength and dexterity.
ideas: thinks it is related to computer work, keyboard ergonomics, or a pinched nerve in the wrist
concerns: worried she might need surgery or that the numbness will become permanent, which would affect her career
expectations: wants advice on wrist splints, ergonomics, or non-surgical treatments
social_hx: works as a software developer, spends 8-10 hours typing daily, non-smoker, plays tennis on weekends

clinical_knowledge.topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: wrist pain and tingling in her fingers

Key HPI features: gradual onset of numbness, tingling, and burning pain in her right hand over the past two months. Affects the thumb, index, and middle fingers. Worse at night, often waking her up, and during long typing sessions at work. Eased by shaking her hand ('flick sign'). No pain in the neck, elbow, or shoulder. Normal grip strength and dexterity.
Objective/Exam findings: Needs hand inspection (thenar atrophy check), sensory testing (median vs ulnar), motor strength (thumb abduction), Phalen's test, and Tinel's sign.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cervical radiculopathy (C6) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Constant numbness or thenar (thumb base) muscle wasting — signals more advanced nerve damage needing urgent referral.
management_principles: Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: AAN Practice Guidelines for Neurological Disorders

reference_soap.subjective: 29F software developer presents with 2-month history of right-hand numbness, tingling, and paresthesia in median nerve distribution (thumb, index, middle fingers). Worse at night and with keyboard use. Positive flick sign. No proximal symptoms, no motor weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Needs hand inspection (thenar atrophy check), sensory testing (median vs ulnar), motor strength (thumb abduction), Phalen's test, and Tinel's sign.
reference_soap.assessment: Mild to moderate Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), right side. DDx: cervical radiculopathy (C6), pronator teres syndrome, de Quervain's tenosynovitis, diabetic neuropathy.
reference_soap.plan: Recommend neutral-angle wrist splint to wear at night and during long typing sessions. Counsel on ergonomic keyboard/mouse adjustments. Discuss short course of NSAIDs. Educate on signs of progression (thenar weakness, constant numbness) that warrant EMG/NCS or surgical referral.

learning_objectives: Elicit symptoms in the classic median nerve distribution
Identify aggravating factors (wrist flexion, typing, sleep positions) and relieving maneuvers (shaking hand)
Explain conservative management options (night splinting, ergonomics) clearly to the patient
Screen for motor deficits (weakness, wasting) and explain when to seek specialist review

teaching.one_liner: Compression of the median nerve at the wrist causes numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers — classically worse at night and relieved by shaking the hand ('flick sign') — usually managed conservatively with a wrist splint first.
red_flags: Constant numbness or thenar (thumb base) muscle wasting — signals more advanced nerve damage needing urgent referral

must_ask.say: Which fingers are affected — your thumb, index, and middle finger?
Does this wake you up at night?
Does shaking your hand make it feel better?
Do you do a lot of typing or repetitive hand work?
Have you noticed any weakness in your grip or dropping things?
